audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 read Skill in both layers while every one of their whys says Zaahen wins outright ('lets you tax a fragile Neeko for free', 'out-trade Neeko decisively', 'you can all-in Neeko whenever you dodge her root', 'you stay ahead'). Row 4 read Zaahen while its why says the stage is even.
audit.why: Neeko has no early durability and no way to answer a melee who dodges Tangle-Barbs; level 6 is the one stage where Pop Blossom's threat evens it. The packet chart and the mirror audit agree on Skill / Zaahen / Zaahen / Zaahen / Skill / Zaahen / Zaahen.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 flipped to Zaahen and row 4 to Skill, all as matched full/content pairs in one group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pop Blossom was described only as needing 'a windup and clone/burst setup', with no cooldown and no mention that the wind-up is hidden while she is disguised.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised.' The whole don't-get-caught advice rests on seeing the wind-up, and against a disguised Neeko that tell does not exist. Pop Blossom is 120/105/90.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] rewritten with the 120s cooldown and the hidden wind-up; breakdown.cooldowns carries both.

audit.whatIsWrong: Inherent Glamour appeared nowhere, and 'E Golden Onslaught' is not one of Zaahen's abilities. Tangle-Barbs's growth mechanic and 12s cooldown were never stated.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: receiving immobilizing crowd control breaks the disguise. Zaahen's Q recast knockup and his W pull are both displacement/immobilizing, so he holds two disguise-breakers — decision-changing and stated nowhere. Tangle-Barbs becomes larger, faster and longer-rooting after it passes through a champion or kills a unit, which is why eating it through the wave is worse than eating it clean.
audit.corrected: Disguise-break added to spikes[1] and report[5].t, Inherent Glamour named in early, Tangle-Barbs's growth and 12s cooldown written into spikes[0], mid, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d. Fabricated E name replaced with a slot reference.

audit.why: Nothing in the brief indicates a recent change to either kit on 26.15.

edits.before: Neeko is a squishy mage top with no early durability; with Q Darkin Glaive and E Golden Onslaught you out-trade and all-in her whenever she steps up to last-hit, and her Tangle-Barbs root is her only real defensive tool to hold.
edits.after: Neeko is a squishy mage top with no early durability; your Q slash and E dash out-trade and all-in her whenever she steps up to last-hit. Tangle-Barbs is 12s at rank 1 and roots for longer once it has passed through a minion or champion first.

edits.before: Neeko R Pop Blossom needs a windup and clone/burst setup to matter, but you keep the edge: gap-close with E through her poke, and if she ults defensively she still can't out-duel your sustained darkin damage.
edits.after: Pop Blossom (R) is 120s at rank 1 and its wind-up is hidden while she is disguised, so the tell you rely on can simply not be there. Your Q knockup and W pull are immobilizing CC and break her disguise outright.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are firmly yours. With Q and E Golden Onslaught you win every trade against a fragile Neeko, and as long as you dodge Tangle-Barbs you can all-in her repeatedly. Her R Pop Blossom doesn't save her from your sustained darkin damage in a 1v1.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are firmly yours. With your Q and E dash you win every trade against a fragile Neeko, and as long as you dodge Tangle-Barbs — 12s at rank 1, growing and rooting longer once it passes through something — you can all-in her repeatedly. Pop Blossom does not save her.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are an even farm start, but from level 2 you already threaten Neeko: she's squishy with no early combat kit beyond poke, so hold Q Darkin Glaive to punish her when she reaches for a minion.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are an even farm start, but from level 2 you already threaten Neeko: she is squishy with no early combat kit beyond poke. Inherent Glamour lets her wear an ally's face, so confirm the champion in front of you is her.

edits.before: - Neeko Tangle-Barbs: matchup-defining — Her root — extends through targets. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Tangle-Barbs (E): matchup-defining — 12s at rank 1, and it roots longer once it has passed through a unit. Dodge it, then commit. - Pop Blossom (R): 120s, and its wind-up is hidden while she is disguised.

edits.before: Her root — extends through targets. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Her root, 12s at rank 1 — it grows through targets. Engage only once it is spent.

edits.before: Track Neeko's Tangle-Barbs: Her root — extends through targets. Dodge it. When it is down — Combo the cooldown gap.
edits.after: Tangle-Barbs: a 12s root that grows after passing through a unit. Your Q knockup and W pull break her disguise.

notes: packet.defects flags 'Pop Blossom's' in whys[4] as a probable wrong ability name at edit distance 2 from 'pop blossom'. It is a FALSE POSITIVE — the distance is just the possessive apostrophe-s. Pop Blossom is the correct name per packet.enemyAbilities and the kit file, and whys[4] is left untouched. Zaahen's E is written by effect ('E dash') rather than a name, because champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json has none and the two mirror auditors disagreed on whether to ship the names from the missing-interactions headlines.
